meta.subtitle: Multi-tenant Supabase / Next.js codebase audit
meta.headline: Tenant isolation holds — no critical or high security exposure. Findings are hardening, performance, and test-quality wins.
meta.authModel: Federated / OAuth-only (no Supabase-managed passwords) — password-related advisors are not applicable.
meta.scope: RLS policies, service-role code paths, API routes, auth/permission layer, migrations, Next.js App Router surface, and the test suite.
meta.methodology: Supabase advisors (security + performance), the D-091 guard suite, vitals (hotspots), knip (dead code), jscpd (duplication), Stryker (mutation testing), and the M9 static detectors. Every finding passes a correctness check (repro/evidence) AND an applicability check (relevant given the app's auth model & exposure).

findings.title: Commission state machine has an untested transition guard
findings.evidence: Stryker: removing the `?.` in `ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS[from]?.has(to)` survived — no test asserts the invalid-from-state path on money-critical logic.
findings.impact: A regression allowing an invalid commission transition would ship undetected.
findings.fix: Add one test asserting an unknown from-state is rejected.

findings.title: 124 unindexed foreign keys
findings.impact: Sequential scans on parent UPDATE/DELETE and FK JOINs; degrades at scale.

findings.title: 50 RLS policies re-evaluate auth.* per row
findings.impact: auth.uid()/auth.role() evaluated per-row instead of once per query.
findings.fix: Wrap in (select …); verified byte-identical (zero semantic drift).

findings.title: 8 data-fetching waterfalls
findings.evidence: check:fetch-waterfalls: independent sequential awaits (confirm no hidden ordering before parallelizing).
findings.impact: Serialized round-trips inflate latency and DB compute on every render.
findings.fix: Promise.all([...]) or a single combined query.

findings.title: server-only poison-pill absent on 43 secret/service-role modules
findings.impact: Currently safe (none client-imported), but no compile-time guard against a future accidental client import bundling a secret.
findings.fix: Add import 'server-only' to the 4 core clients (transitively covers most). Requires the server-only dependency.

findings.title: 27 pages opt into dynamic rendering
findings.evidence: check:dynamic-rendering: searchParams/headers()/cookies()/force-dynamic. Mostly intended for authed pages — needs per-page confirmation.
findings.fix: Confirm each is intentionally dynamic; statically render where possible.

findings.title: RLS-no-policy: 11/13 confirmed locked; tier_definitions & pricing_seat_ladder have a SELECT grant with no policy
findings.evidence: Checked client grants: 11 of 13 have NO anon/authenticated SELECT grant → deny-all by design, confirmed service-role-only (no action). tier_definitions & pricing_seat_ladder DO grant SELECT to anon/authenticated but have no policy — the grant says readable, RLS returns empty.
findings.impact: 11 confirmed safe. The 2 have a grant/policy mismatch: either a vestigial grant, or a client read that's silently returning empty (functional, not a leak — these are RLS-enabled, so nothing is exposed).
findings.fix: For tier_definitions & pricing_seat_ladder, pick one: DROP the anon/authenticated SELECT grant (if server-only) OR add the intended SELECT policy (if client-readable). Separately, tidy the over-broad TRUNCATE/REFERENCES grants to anon/authenticated (not API-reachable, but unnecessary).
findings.okWhen: the SELECT grant is vestigial and these tables are genuinely server-only → drop the grant for clarity.
findings.notOkWhen: a client/pricing page is meant to read tiers/seats directly → the policy is missing and that read returns empty → add the SELECT policy.

findings.title: 62 unused exports + 75 unused exported types
findings.evidence: knip (review before pruning — some may be public API / dynamically referenced / framework entry points).
findings.impact: Dead surface area; onboarding & search noise.

findings.title: tenant_is_active() is RPC-callable with no caller check (2 sibling definer helpers are caller-scoped — OK)
findings.evidence: Read each function body: auth_user_in_tenant + auth_user_can_access_conversation constrain by auth.uid() (caller-scoped — cleared); tenant_is_active filters ONLY by its target_tenant_id parameter, no caller check. (Advisor flagged all three; body analysis narrowed it to one.)
findings.impact: Any signed-in user can probe whether an ARBITRARY tenant ID exists / is active (minor enumeration). The other two reveal only the caller's own access — no action needed.
findings.fix: tenant_is_active: add a caller constraint, or REVOKE EXECUTE from authenticated/anon (policies invoke it as definer, so RLS is unaffected by the revoke). Leave the other two as-is.

findings.title: 86 unused indexes
findings.evidence: Supabase advisor: unused_index (since last stats reset — verify per index before dropping).
findings.fix: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY after per-index review (risk: dropping a rarely-used-but-needed index).
findings.okWhen: the index has had zero scans across a representative window (covers your monthly/seasonal + admin jobs), it isn't enforcing a UNIQUE constraint, and no planned feature needs it. Then dropping reclaims write/storage overhead safely.
findings.notOkWhen: stats were recently reset (short window), the index backs a rare-but-critical path (admin export, end-of-month reconcile) that hasn't run, or it enforces uniqueness — dropping it is then a latent regression. Verify each before dropping.

findings.title: 4.4% duplicated lines (465 clones)
findings.evidence: jscpd (some clones may be intentional — generated code / fixtures).
findings.impact: Maintenance tax: a fix in one clone misses the others.
findings.fix: Consolidate opportunistically (full dedup is multi-week — hence low BFTB).

findings.title: app/api/chat/route.ts is the #1 hotspot
findings.evidence: vitals: health 2.4, 41 changes/90d, co-changes with 29 files.
findings.impact: Central, churny, complex — a future-bug magnet with wide blast radius.
findings.fix: Decompose into modules. High value but slow & risky — schedule as a planned refactor, not a quick win.

findings.title: Leaked-password protection disabled
findings.impact: Would matter if email/password auth were used.
findings.note: Not applicable — the app uses federated/OAuth auth exclusively, so there are no Supabase-managed passwords. Checked and ruled out via the auth questionnaire (applicability gate).
